newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai to continue tight monetary policy in H2.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai to continue tight monetary policy in H2.

text.p: Shanghai, China's richest city and its mercantile hub, will maintain its tight monetary policy and strict control over bank loans throughout 1997, the head of the local central bank branch was reported as saying.

Mao Yingliang, quoted in Thursday's Shanghai Securities News, said Shanghai's financial institutions needed to develop new means of lending money, such as syndicated loans, and to improve loan structure.
Financial institutions should improve control of cash flow and strictly control money supply, Mao was quoted as saying.
Shanghai would strictly prevent bank money flowing into the stock markets and avoid irregular deposits and loans, Mao said.
The Shenzhen Development Bank was recently punished by regulators for using bank money to trade its own stock on the Shanghai bourse.
Local banks would also improve the way they helped foreign banks in Shanghai do local currency business, he said.
Nine foreign banks have been approved to do local currency business in Shanghai.
